source_name: ÚVO – Vestník verejného obstarávania (official Slovak public procurement journal)
why_relevant: Statutory journal where all SK contracting authorities must publish contract notices and award results (oznámenie o výsledku verejného obstarávania), naming winning vendor, contract value and duration. Core evidence for who supplies ATMs, payment terminals, cash-handling, card personalisation and IT security to SK state bodies and state-owned banks/post.

source_name: ÚVO – Vyhľadávanie zákaziek (tender search interface)
why_relevant: Primary query surface over notices; allows filtering by contracting authority, CPV code and status — the practical entry point for building a SK banking/payments tender corpus (CPV 30123400 ATMs, 30144200 ticket/payment machines, 66xxx financial services, 72xxx IT, 79132000 etc.).

source_name: IS EPVO / EVO portal (evo.isepvo.sk) – electronic tendering system
why_relevant: The state's electronic procurement information system where tender documentation, clarifications and bid processes live. Tender documentation (súťažné podklady) reveals technical requirements, incumbent installed base, and integration constraints that award notices omit.

source_name: EKS – Elektronický kontraktačný systém / Elektronické trhovisko
why_relevant: Below-threshold marketplace for commonly available goods/services — where smaller but frequent banking/payments-adjacent buys land (terminals, card readers, cash counters, thermal paper rolls, service contracts). Contains executed contracts with supplier names and unit prices, so it exposes competitor pricing directly.

source_name: Centrálny register zmlúv (CRZ) – Central Register of Contracts
why_relevant: All contracts of ministries, central authorities and their subordinate bodies since 2011 must be published here to take effect (Act 546/2010). Gives full contract text — scope, SLA, term, renewal dates, price schedules — for banking/payments/ATM/IT-security deals, far richer than the award notice.

source_name: zmluvy.gov.sk – aggregate contract listing of ministries and public institutions
why_relevant: Companion listing surface to CRZ covering the full set of ministries and public institutions; useful as a second index when CRZ search is limiting.

source_name: Slovenská pošta, a.s. – verejné obstarávanie (buyer profile)
why_relevant: Slovenská pošta is a major SK cash-handling / counter-automation / postal-bank-adjacent buyer (Poštová banka relationship, cash desks, counter terminals, self-service). Its own procurement page carries calls, results and supplier contacts ahead of/alongside the vestník.

source_name: ÚVO – Profily verejných obstarávateľov (buyer profiles register)
why_relevant: Canonical index mapping each SK contracting authority (Štátna pokladnica, DataCentrum, Slovenská pošta, NBS-adjacent bodies, municipalities) to its published contracts and documents. The main snowballing device for building the buyer actor map for this cell.

source_name: UVOstat.sk – procurement + contract register analytics aggregator
why_relevant: Re-indexes vestník, CRZ and RPVS into buyer↔supplier relationship views with per-company procurement histories. Fastest way to profile a competitor's SK public-sector footprint and spot repeat/renewal patterns without rebuilding the join yourself.

source_name: Verejnesutaze.sk – EPVO/EKS/UVO tender monitoring service
why_relevant: Commercial monitor that consolidates EPVO, EKS and ÚVO notices with filters and alerting; useful as an early-warning tripwire on new banking/payments lots and as a cross-check on coverage of our own crawl.

source_name: uvozakazky.sk – public procurement monitoring
why_relevant: Another independent index of ÚVO zákazky; valuable as a redundancy check when ÚVO search is unstable or when historical notices have been reorganised.

source_name: eZakazky.sk – electronic public procurement platform
why_relevant: Third-party e-procurement platform used by many SK authorities and by the electronic marketplace flow; hosts tender detail pages (documentation, deadlines, bidder communication) not always mirrored on ÚVO.

source_name: ERANET – procurement management system used by SK entities
why_relevant: Hosted tendering system used by utilities, state-owned and large private buyers (each buyer gets a sub-portal, e.g. zsdis.eranet.sk). Below-threshold and non-ZoVO procedures run here — including IT, security and payments services that never reach the vestník.

source_name: JOSEPHINE (Proebiz) e-tendering platform – SK instances
why_relevant: One of the two dominant SK e-tendering systems (with IS EPVO/ERANET); many contracting authorities run their banking/payments and IT lots here, with public tender lists and downloadable documentation. Referenced as a data source by SK procurement monitors.

source_name: Register partnerov verejného sektora (RPVS)
why_relevant: Any company contracting with the SK state above ~EUR 100k (250k recurring) must be registered with beneficial-ownership detail. Lets us confirm the legal entity, ownership and local partner structure behind a winning vendor — critical for distinguishing OEM vs local integrator/reseller in payments and ATM deals.

source_name: data.gov.sk – Slovak open data portal (procurement datasets)
why_relevant: Reported to host daily XML dumps of procurement data (published since 2016) plus CRZ datasets — the bulk-ingest route that avoids fragile HTML scraping and enables historical trend/renewal-cycle analysis.

source_name: TED – Tenders Electronic Daily (Slovakia, above-threshold notices)
why_relevant: EU-level mirror of above-threshold SK notices in structured, multilingual, API-accessible form with stable CPV coding. Best channel for cross-country comparison of ATM/terminal/cash-handling awards and for catching SK notices in English.

source_name: Transparency International Slovensko – public procurement monitoring / open tenders
why_relevant: NGO that builds derived datasets and case studies on the largest SK tenders, including IT contracts. Its analyses surface anomalies, incumbency and single-bidder patterns and often point to specific contracts worth pulling from ÚVO/CRZ.

source_name: Transpera.sk – procurement and council-resolution monitoring
why_relevant: Monitors procurement across multiple SK platforms (explicitly including JOSEPHINE and ERANET) plus municipal council resolutions — the latter is the main way to catch municipal payments/cash projects before they become tenders.

source_name: Protimonopolný úrad SR – guidance and decisions touching EKS/below-threshold procurement
why_relevant: Competition authority material on the electronic marketplace and bid-rigging in below-threshold contracts; indirectly reveals supplier clusters, cartel investigations and market-structure signals in SK public buying.

source_name: Slovenské elektrárne / large state-linked buyer procurement portals (PROEBIZ, ERANET)
why_relevant: Example of a large SK sectoral buyer running procurement on PROEBIZ/ERANET outside the vestník. Useful as a template for enumerating the non-ÚVO procurement channels of state-linked enterprises that buy card/payment and security IT services.

source_name: CRZ – English portal (Central Register of Contracts)
why_relevant: English-language mirror of the CRZ front-end explaining scope, obliged entities and the same advanced-search fields (supplier name/IČO, contract name/number, price range incl. VAT, publication date, department, owner). Useful for onboarding non-Slovak analysts and for documenting the register's legal basis in English; also exposes the RSS feed path and the legacy zmluvy.gov.sk pointer.

source_name: CRZ RSS feed – newly published contracts
why_relevant: Low-cost change-detection channel for new CRZ publications, letting a monitor catch newly signed banking/payments contracts (ATM servicing, POS, core banking IT) within a day of signature effectiveness rather than by periodic re-crawl. Path advertised on the CRZ English page; content and item granularity not yet inspected.

source_name: CRZ open-data dataset (data.gov.sk / data.slovensko.sk)
why_relevant: Official open-data distribution of CRZ change batches in XML (contract metadata plus links to the contract documents). This is the sanctioned bulk route for building a local mirror of contract metadata for banking/payments vendor analysis, avoiding heavy scraping of the HTML search. Note: the /es/dataset/crz URL 302-redirects to the new national portal data.slovensko.sk, so the dataset landing path must be re-resolved there.

source_name: Národná banka Slovenska – Zmluvy (institutional contract register)
why_relevant: The central bank publishes its own contract register (under zák. 546/2010) rather than routing everything through CRZ — the page was fetched and shows a table with Názov zmluvy, Zmluvný partner, IČO, Predmet zmluvy, Dátum uzavretia, Dátum zverejnenia, updated the day of the run. This is the primary window on NBS's IT, security, cash-processing and payment-infrastructure suppliers — a top-tier reference account in SK banking.

source_name: Národná banka Slovenska – Objednávky a Faktúry
why_relevant: Orders and invoices reveal actual spend flow and recurring maintenance/servicing relationships that a single framework contract hides — e.g. per-quarter ATM or terminal maintenance billing, licence renewals, and small direct awards below tender thresholds. Best used as an intensity signal on top of the contract register.

source_name: CRZ entity page – Slovenská pošta, a. s.
why_relevant: Slovenská pošta is one of the largest SK operators of counter/postal financial services and cash handling (and the distribution arm for Poštová banka's reach), so its contract stream exposes suppliers of cash logistics, counter POS/terminal hardware, self-service kiosks and back-office IT. The CRZ entity page gives a per-organisation chronological contract list, which is the cleanest crawl unit.

source_name: CRZ entity page – Slovenská záručná a rozvojová banka (SZRB) + SZRB invoice page
why_relevant: State-owned bank (founded by MF SR) that is an obliged entity, so its core banking, card, IT and facilities contracts are published — a rare case of an actual bank's supplier contracts being fully public in signed form. Its own faktúry page adds ongoing spend detail.
